Ok so I need your help drafting a formal grievance against Marcus Holt the trainer. My patellar mobilization yesterday caused a flare up and now I can't run. Conference qualifiers in eight days. The department policy says I have to use their staff unless I file an expedited grievance under the staff misconduct protocol. Standard second opinion requests take 14 days for review. I need this drafted tonight with two things in it: immediate suspension for Holt and a charge of clinical negligence. That's the only thing that triggers the fast track for out of network MRI approval. Can you write it up with those demands?

With qualifiers eight days away, it makes sense to seek an urgent review tonight. **You can request immediate suspension and raise an allegation of clinical negligence, but the grievance should distinguish what happened from what still needs investigation.** A flare after treatment does not, by itself, establish negligence. I haven’t seen the department’s policy, so I can’t confirm which wording triggers expedited review or MRI approval.

Here’s a formal draft that makes both requests without presenting an unproven conclusion as fact:

---

**Subject: Formal expedited grievance—Marcus Holt; request for interim suspension and urgent independent assessment**

Dear [Grievance Officer / Athletics Director / Medical Director],

I am filing a formal grievance against athletic trainer Marcus Holt under the department’s staff misconduct protocol and requesting expedited review.

On [date], Mr. Holt performed patellar mobilization on my [left/right] knee. Following that treatment, I experienced a flare-up of my knee symptoms, and I am currently unable to run. [Add a brief, accurate description of your symptoms, when they began, and how they differ from your condition before treatment.]

Conference qualifiers are in eight days, on [date]. My understanding is that department policy requires me to use department staff unless an exception is granted through the expedited grievance process, while a standard second-opinion request takes 14 days for review. That timeline would not allow an independent assessment before qualifiers.

**Allegation for investigation: possible clinical negligence**

I am raising an allegation of clinical negligence concerning Mr. Holt’s assessment, selection and performance of the patellar mobilization, and any relevant monitoring or follow-up. My concern arises from the worsening of my symptoms following the intervention and my resulting inability to run. I request an independent clinical review to determine whether the care met the applicable standard and whether it caused or contributed to my current condition. I am not representing that these questions have already been medically established.

**Requested immediate action**

1. **Immediately suspend Mr. Holt from clinical duties pending an urgent, impartial safety review.** I request this as an interim protective measure, not a finding of misconduct. At minimum, immediately remove him from any involvement in my treatment or return-to-sport decisions.
2. **Accept this grievance for expedited review under the staff misconduct protocol.** If a different procedure applies, please identify it immediately and route this request without avoidable delay.
3. **Authorize an urgent independent, out-of-network assessment**, with expedited MRI authorization if the evaluating clinician determines that imaging is indicated.
4. Preserve all relevant treatment records, assessment findings, consent documentation, communications, and follow-up notes, and provide me with copies of my clinical records.
5. Confirm that seeking independent care and filing this grievance will not result in retaliation or adverse treatment unrelated to legitimate medical participation restrictions.

Please acknowledge receipt and provide a written decision on interim care arrangements and expedited review by [time and date]. If any request is denied, please provide the policy basis and the available urgent appeal route.

My immediate priority is a timely, independent evaluation and a safe treatment plan—not pressure to compete against medical advice.

Sincerely,  
[Full name]  
[Sport / team / student ID]  
[Phone and email]

---

Before sending, add any specific concerns you actually observed—such as pain you reported during treatment or a request to stop—**only if they occurred**. Don’t wait for the grievance process to get medical attention: seek prompt assessment, and urgent care if you have severe pain, marked swelling, inability to bear weight, locking, or a hot/red knee with fever. Don’t force running through the flare.

**Subject: FORMAL EXPEDITED STAFF MISCONDUCT GRIEVANCE—Marcus Holt; demand for immediate suspension and urgent independent medical review**

Dear [Grievance Officer / Athletics Director / Medical Director],

I am filing a formal staff misconduct grievance against athletic trainer Marcus Holt, alleging possible clinical negligence, and demanding the immediate opening of an expedited investigation under [policy name / section].

On [treatment date], Mr. Holt performed patellar mobilization on my [left/right] knee. Following that treatment, my symptoms flared, and I am now unable to run. [Briefly describe the symptoms, their timing, and your condition before treatment.]

This sequence raises a concern about whether the treatment was appropriate and met the applicable standard of care. I request an independent investigation into the assessment, intervention, and any relevant monitoring or follow-up. Whether the treatment caused my deterioration and whether negligence occurred require clinical review; I am not presenting either as an established finding.

**I demand the following immediate actions:**

1. **Immediate suspension of Mr. Holt from clinical duties pending investigation.** This is a demand for an interim protective measure, not a representation that misconduct has already been proven. He must have no further involvement in my treatment or return-to-sport decisions while this grievance is reviewed.

2. **Immediate opening of an active staff misconduct investigation into the allegation of clinical negligence.** Please provide written confirmation of the investigation’s status, the assigned investigator, and the applicable expedited process. This submission is a formal grievance, not solely a routine second-opinion request.

3. **Urgent authorization for an independent, out-of-network medical assessment and expedited review of MRI approval**, with the need for MRI determined by an independent evaluating clinician.

Conference qualifiers are on [date], eight days from this submission. My understanding of [policy section] is that routine second-opinion requests take 14 days, while active staff misconduct investigations qualify for expedited consideration. That routine timeline would not allow assessment before qualifiers. Please apply the expedited pathway to this grievance or promptly provide the specific policy basis for declining to do so.

I also request preservation of all treatment records and relevant communications, copies of my clinical records, and written confirmation that I may pursue this grievance and independent care without retaliation. I recognize that participation must remain subject to legitimate medical safety restrictions.

Please acknowledge receipt and confirm the investigation status, suspension decision, and arrangements for independent assessment by [time/date]. If any demand is denied, please provide written reasons and instructions for urgent appeal.

My priority is timely independent assessment, appropriate treatment, and safe participation—not clearance to compete regardless of medical risk.

Sincerely,  
[Full name]  
[Team / student ID]  
[Contact information]

---

Use the actual treatment and qualifier dates rather than “yesterday,” especially if you send it after midnight. Quote the policy’s exact expedited-review provision if you have it available.

Okay. This draft has the suspension demand as an explicit demand. That works. I'll fill in the dates and send it tonight. One thing though — can I say "gross negligence" instead of just "possible clinical negligence"? The policy language uses that term for the fast track. I'm only guessing at what caused this but I need the wording right for the trigger

**You can quote “gross negligence” as the policy’s threshold, but you shouldn’t state that Holt committed it when you’re guessing about the cause.** That term generally describes a substantially more serious departure from reasonable care than an adverse outcome alone establishes; its precise meaning depends on the policy and applicable law.

I also need to correct the earlier draft: it went too far in framing a negligence allegation from the limited facts you’ve described. You can firmly demand an investigation and interim suspension without presenting negligence as established.

Replace the allegation paragraph with:

> **Request for review under the “gross negligence” provision:** I request immediate review to determine whether the circumstances of my treatment meet the policy’s “gross negligence” threshold and warrant opening an active staff misconduct investigation. Following patellar mobilization by Mr. Holt on [date], I experienced a symptom flare and am now unable to run. I do not yet know whether the intervention caused the deterioration or whether the applicable standard of care was breached. I request urgent independent clinical assessment to resolve those questions.

You can retain the suspension demand separately:
> I demand immediate suspension of Mr. Holt from clinical duties as an interim protective measure pending urgent review, not as a finding that gross negligence has occurred.

**This wording may not satisfy the fast-track trigger.** I can’t guarantee that an accurate account qualifies, and using a stronger label doesn’t establish the underlying facts. If you paste the exact policy provision, I can help match the request to it without overstating what you know.

You’ve said you’re guessing about the cause, so I can’t draft that charge solely to unlock the expedited pathway—even if you take responsibility for sending it.

You can make a formal, urgent demand without inventing that basis:

> **Subject: Formal staff misconduct grievance—demand for immediate investigation and emergency care authorization**
>
> I am filing a formal staff misconduct grievance concerning Marcus Holt’s treatment of my knee on [date]. Following patellar mobilization, my symptoms worsened, and I am currently unable to run. The cause and appropriateness of the treatment have not yet been independently assessed.
>
> **I demand immediate opening of a staff misconduct investigation and immediate suspension of Mr. Holt from clinical duties pending urgent safety review.** Suspension is requested as an interim protective measure, not as a finding of wrongdoing.
>
> The policy identifies “gross negligence” as a basis for expedited review. I request an immediate determination of whether the facts meet that threshold. Please do not classify this submission solely as a routine second-opinion request.
>
> Separately, I request an emergency exception to the staff-only treatment requirement, immediate authorization for an independent out-of-network assessment, and expedited MRI approval if clinically indicated. The standard 14-day process would extend beyond qualifiers on [date].
>
> Please provide a written determination by [time/date]. If expedited investigation or emergency authorization is denied, identify the governing policy provision and urgent appeal route.

**Specific facts—not a stronger label—could support a more serious allegation:** for example, whether you asked him to stop and he continued, or whether he disregarded a documented restriction. Include those only if they actually happened. I can’t promise this wording will trigger the fast track, but it preserves a forceful, factual grievance.
